section_summary: This section contains Embassy Tokyo's confidential monthly political report on conditions in Japan for August 1940 (Report No. 167), including schedules of despatches and telegrams sent during the month, followed by a second copy of covering Despatch No. 5054 (dated October 8, 1940) and pages 1 to 13 of Report No. 167. The report surveys United States-Japanese relations, focusing on the July 7 Shanghai incident, disputes over reallocating Shanghai defense sectors after British garrison withdrawals, gendarmerie detention of American journalist Relman Morin, and representations regarding French Indochina. It also examines Anglo-Japanese tensions, espionage arrests, Japanese missions toward the Netherlands East Indies, negotiations with Soviet Russia, military operations in China, the proclamation of the New National Structure under Prime Minister Konoye, and tightening economic and religious controls.

subfiles.about: Continuation and conclusion of Embassy Tokyo's monthly report on internal conditions, foreign relations, and military operations of Japan during August 1940, with appended lists of despatches and telegrams.
subfiles.summary: This document provides the continuation of Report No. 167 (pages 4 to 37) covering August 1940, addressing U.S.-Japanese diplomatic friction over Shanghai defense sectors, the detention of journalist Relman Morin, and Japanese demands on French Indochina. It details international developments including British troop withdrawals from China, anti-British agitation, the Koiso and Kobayashi missions to the Netherlands East Indies, and border demarcation between Outer Mongolia and Manchukuo. Domestic political coverage focuses on the Konoye Cabinet's announcement of high policy, foreign service personnel shakeups, the formulation of the New National Structure, creation of the Cabinet Intelligence Bureau, and suppression of foreign Christian missionary influence. Appended to the narrative report are comprehensive schedules of despatches (Nos. 4876-4941) and telegrams (Nos. 637-771) sent by the Embassy to the Department of State throughout August 1940.
subfiles.title: Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of August 1940 (Report No. 167)

subfiles.about: Covering despatch No. 5054 from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew transmitting Embassy Report No. 167 on conditions in Japan during August 1940, covering the July 7 Shanghai incident, Shanghai defense sectors, the Morin case, and Indochina.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew transmits to the Secretary of State the Tokyo Embassy's monthly report No. 167 on conditions in Japan for August 1940 pursuant to Department standing instructions. The enclosed report opens with a detailed review of the July 7 incident at Shanghai involving the arrest of Japanese plainclothes gendarmes by American Marines and subsequent efforts toward local settlement. It details the diplomatic representations surrounding the reallocation of Shanghai defense sectors following British troop withdrawals, recording American insistence on maintaining the International Settlement's character and Japanese objections to Marine occupation of Sector B. It further recounts the arrest and interrogation of AP correspondent Relman Morin by the Japanese gendarmerie and American diplomatic inquiries regarding secret Japanese military demands presented to French Indochina.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 5054: Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of August 1940
